### Assistant · 2026-10-09 12:24:11

I've sent the orchestrator my final acceptance view: the store is not ready to publish. Two owner blockers and one theme defect remain. The full report is in [qa/FINAL-ACCEPTANCE.md](qa/FINAL-ACCEPTANCE.md).

**Blockers, ranked by shopper impact:**
1. **Payments are not set up.** Checkout opens and shows the order total, but nobody can pay. This is an owner step.
2. **The refund policy page shows the shipping policy text.** It is linked from checkout and visible to search engines. This is also an owner fix.
3. **Journal stories are unreadable on phones.** At 390 px the first slide's text runs under the nail art on every article. This goes to st-foundation.

**Hero:** the v2.2 install passes everything I re-checked on the preview. I found one new desktop defect. At 1280, the Wild Card and Diet Cherry characters covered the first letters of the headline, and the left-side characters sat under the shop button. I fixed it as v2.3 with a CSS-only change to [motion/st-hero.css](motion/st-hero.css). It is clean in the lab at 1180, 1280 and 1440, and phones are unchanged. St-foundation still needs to copy the file over.

**SEO implementation:** passes on the preview. Three description fixes are still needed:
- The Help page description promises returns information that the page hides.
- The talks page description promises a way to send submissions, but the page has no form.
- The home page title and description still say "Almond" and "original illustrated packaging". This is an owner step in Shopify preferences.

**Checked and working:**
- Add to bag, cart quantity changes and reaching checkout.
- Search results and the no-results page.
- Help form labels, the 404 page, and alt attributes on every image.

**Couldn't be confirmed in the browser pane:**
- Menu drawer focus and Escape behaviour.
- Content further down the home page at desktop width.
- The Journal slide counter.

**Not tested:** real devices, reduced motion, the theme editor, payment, and sending the contact form.

Once the v2.3 copy and the Journal fix are installed, I'll re-check both on the preview.

The first preview acceptance is done and reported to the orchestrator. On the landing page, 13 sections pass, 2 need fixing and 1 has a minor spacing issue. The hero passes apart from two items now fixed in hero v3.2, which is frozen and ready to copy. The report is in [qa/fidelity/LANDING-PREVIEW-1.md](qa/fidelity/LANDING-PREVIEW-1.md).

**Landing fixes.** Both were caused by the review-3 changes. I measured them on the live preview:
- **Brainwave:** the character shows as a 69 px sliver. She is drawn about half the size she should be and shifted out of her clipping box. I sent st-foundation the target size and position.
- **Green Flag:** the phone art has vanished. The softened edges are now correct, but the image sits roughly 760 px above the box that clips it, so nothing shows. Moving it down fixes it.
- **Minor:** the FAQ rows are now about 50 px apart, against roughly 41 on the board.

**Hero on the preview.**
- All seven sets match my test-page renders side by side.
- Skin tones swap without moving the nail, and the layouts at 320, 430 and 1280 are clean with no console errors.
- St-foundation's theme code follows the hero contract, and the fonts load correctly.
- The words in the headline still run together. The word-spacing fix (v3.1) is included in v3.2.

**A real bug I found and fixed.** A tap on the preview hand during the hero's first second, while the first set is still loading, was ignored. Autoplay started afterwards and cancelled the tap. On a slow phone, a shopper's first tap would be lost. In v3.2 the hero keeps the shopper's choice. I verified it on my test page: the tap moves to the next set, it's announced to screen readers, and autoplay stays off.

**Fixes needed:**

The owner's earlier packaging rule also asks for loose nails in shop tiles. The fix is to shift the box left and add three of the set's own nails on the right.
- **Tile colours:** the board's tiles are noticeably brighter than the hero background colours the spec prescribed. Diet Cherry is the most visible case: bright red on the board, dark red in the build. I sent my samples and asked for the spec to be corrected from the board.
- **Last card:** on the board, the single Pinky Promise card at the bottom is wider and its name fits on one line. In the build it's the same width as the others and the name wraps.

The first two fixes together are why the build's grid looks paler and emptier than the board.

**Passing:** the header, the heading and its handwritten note, the filter chips, the grid spacing, names, prices, "View set" links, the footer, the desktop layout and accessibility.

The filter chips work. Everyday shows 4 sets and Statement shows 3, and both tag pages are correctly hidden from search.

### Assistant · 2026-10-09 19:17:30

The bag page is reviewed: 10 elements pass and 2 need fixing. I also settled the font question st-boardspec raised about the subtotal. The report is in [qa/fidelity/BAG-PREVIEW-1.md](qa/fidelity/BAG-PREVIEW-1.md), and the orchestrator has it.

**Subtotal font:** both the "Subtotal" label and the amount should use IBM Plex Sans Condensed Bold at about 24 px, in navy. At 2x zoom the board's "Subtotal" has no serifs, so the serif label in the build is the wrong family. I compared the word's width-to-height ratio against each candidate font:

| Font | Ratio |
|---|---|
| Board ink, after allowing for blur | about 4.7–4.8 |
| IBM Plex Sans Condensed Bold | 4.85 |
| Barlow Semi Condensed Bold | 4.76 |
| Source Serif 4 Bold, current | 5.14 |
| DM Sans Bold | 5.69 |

Plex at 24 px makes the word about 87 px wide, which matches the board. I asked for the spec to be corrected.

**Fixes:**
- **Subtotal:** switch the label to Plex and raise both the label and amount to 24 px.
- **Promo heading:** "Nails for every plot twist." is about 15% too small. Raising it to about 30 px makes it span the width it does on the board.

**Passing:**
- **Page top:** the header, the "Your bag" title and the item count.
- **Line items:** the tiles, names, prices, quantity buttons and Remove links match. Their spacing is wider than the board's to keep 44 px tap targets, which I accepted.
- **Checkout:** the Checkout button and the "Continue shopping" link.
- **Lower panels:** the help panel has placeholder character art, and the pink promo panel with its four nails matches apart from the heading size.
- **Other views:** the footer, the empty-bag state and the desktop layout.

**Minor:** the quantity minus sign is light grey at quantity 1, while the board shows it dark. That's fine if it marks a real disabled state.

Next, I re-check these two bag fixes and the product page's narrow-phone fix once st-foundation re-shoots them.

   - Arc headline: split into lines, words and letters, aria-hidden; visually hidden full text; kerning restored with Range measurements; radius 380 board px × k.
   - Fonts: Fraunces 900 SOFT100 WONK1 opsz144 (hero), Fraunces 700 SOFT50 (chapters), Caveat 700, Barlow Semi Condensed 600, Source Serif 4 Black/Italic, IBM Plex Sans Condensed 700 (card names, prices, subtotal), DM Sans, Kalam.

      const flyer = this.makeFlyer(sprite, col, b.w, b.h);
      const s0 = b.w ? a.w / b.w : 1;
      const liftPx = -Math.min(72, b.h * lift);
      const mid = { x: (a.x + b.x) / 2, y: (a.y + b.y) / 2 + (arc ? liftPx : 0) };
      const frames = [
        { transform: this.transformAt(a, b.w, b.h, a.rot, s0), easing: 'cubic-bezier(.4,0,.6,1)' },

        { transform: this.transformAt(b, b.w, b.h, b.rot, 1) },

Hero v3.6 is frozen and sent to [Small Talk — Orchestrator](#local_e4896004-68cd-4d55-9d37-ab925783b63b). It switches to st-artwork's fixed HD nail sheets without st-artwork's proposed scale change. Board 2 frame 1 (On Me) is the reference:

| Main nail on On Me at 390 | Finger width at cuticle | Press-on width |
|---|---|---|
| Board | ~170 px | 122 px |
| Live v3.4 | ~190 px | 130 px |
| v3.5 (HD finger, old sheets) | ~177 px | 130 px |
| **v3.6 (HD finger, HD sheets)** | ~177 px | **123 px** |
| st-artwork's physical fit | ~177 px | ~113 px |

**Is v3.5's nail too wide?** Yes, about 7% wider than the board. The old sheets' plates fill more of their frame, and our nail is already a little larger relative to the finger than st-artwork assumed. Relative to the HD finger, the gap is only about 2%. I'll confirm on the preview once v3.5 is installed.

**Can the HD sheets go in as v3.6?** Yes. The fixed sheets are clean: every nail's base sits on the cuticle point, plates are centred, the stray specks are gone, and column order matches the old sheets. With the existing scale, the press-on comes out at 123 px, matching the board. st-artwork's physical fit would make it 7% narrower than the board, so I didn't use it.

**What changes in v3.6:**
- The stylesheet changes one line: the two loose nails go from 78 to 82 so they keep their accepted size.
- The preview hand needs nothing; the new plates still cover the hand's natural nails.
- The controller code is unchanged since v3.4.
- For st-foundation, it's a data swap: every set's nail sheet, the first-load nail images and the preload all point to the HD files.

The composite [hero-v36-main-nail-vs-board.png](qa/fidelity/hero-v36-main-nail-vs-board.png) shows no bare-nail crescent; notes are in [HERO-V36.md](qa/fidelity/HERO-V36.md).

I told [Small Talk — Orchestrator](#local_e4896004-68cd-4d55-9d37-ab925783b63b) to use the HD nail sheets on every surface, with no accepted omissions. That covers the landing chapters and tiles, shop cards, Journal close-ups, the product-page scene, the bag and the talks avatars.

**Why:** I measured nail sizes on the preview at 390. Five surfaces render the old sheets at less detail than a 3× phone screen needs:

| Surface | Nail width | Old sheets | HD sheets |
|---|---|---|---|
| Landing chapter rows | 77 px | 2.65× | 5.8× |
| Journal close-ups | ~100+ px | ~2× | ~4.5× |
| Bag | 74 px | ~2.8× | ~6× |
| Product-page scene | ~70 px | ~3× | ~6× |
| Talks thread avatar | 92 px | 2.2× | ~4.9× |
| Shop cards | 34–38 px | 5.4–6× | little visible gain |

The deciding point for shop cards is caching. The hero already loads the HD sheets, so keeping old sheets anywhere means visitors download both versions of each set's nails. One HD file per set gets downloaded once and reused on every page.

**Scale rule:** on every surface except the hero, the nail frames grow by 1.058× around the same base point. Visible nail widths then stay exactly as already accepted: the chapter rows keep 69 px nails with 3 px gaps. The HD nails come out 5.8% longer at the tip, which is closer to the board's proportions. The hero is excluded because v3.6 and v3.7 already fit it to the board.

**After the install I'll check:**
- the longer tips in the chapter rows clear the headline above;
- the shop-card nails still sit on their tray art;
- no crop on the other surfaces clips the longer tips;
- everything looks crisp at 3×.

I froze hero v3.7.1 and answered all four QA items. The message to [Small Talk — Orchestrator](#local_e4896004-68cd-4d55-9d37-ab925783b63b) is queued while that session finishes a turn. The full spec is [QA-OPS-RESPONSE-1.md](qa/fidelity/QA-OPS-RESPONSE-1.md), and the HTML template changes for st-foundation are in the contract. I'd already re-accepted v3.7 earlier, and that report stands.

**1. Slow home-page load.** The large image that counts as the main paint, the finger, arrives 8–9 seconds into a slow-phone test. The hero caused part of that in two ways:
- At start-up the controller fetched the next set's nail images straight away.
- Autoplay started early and pulled later states' art into the same window.

v3.7.1 fixes both:
- The next set's nails load only after the finger image arrives.
- Autoplay and later states' art wait until the page has finished loading.

For st-foundation:
- Preload only the finger image and the first set's nails.
- Mark everything below the hero as low priority.
- Skip off-screen layout work on the lower home-page sections.
- Trim the web fonts.
- Find what triggers a 0.61 MB Shopify checkout prefetch on the home page.

The target is the finger finishing about 1.2 s after first paint, roughly 3–3.5 s in the same test instead of 8.8 s. A real PageSpeed run should confirm it.

**2. Main-thread blocking and the slow menu tap.** I profiled the hero live: start-up takes 12 ms, a set change 15–26 ms, and the curved headline 6–17 ms. So the hero isn't the source of the 0.8–0.9 s blocking tasks; those point to large platform and theme script bundles, and I named the likely ones. The hero's real cost was redrawing the curved headline every time one of about ten web fonts finished loading. v3.7.1 makes these changes:
- That redraw happens once, and only for the headline font.
- After each set change, the headline redraw moves to the next frame, so the work splits into two shorter tasks.
- Autoplay starts after page load.
- Animation pauses while the menu, bag or search panel is open.

**3. Accessibility.** The press-and-hold nail button also works from the keyboard, so it has to stay reachable. The fix is a template change: stop hiding the finger wrapper from screen readers, and hide only the finger image. No code change.

**4. Rotating headline as the page's main heading.** This is acceptable as it stands. The SEO strategy already accepts it: the page title carries the category, and there is exactly one main heading at all times.

### Assistant · 2026-10-10 10:06:54

I accepted all five checks on the v3.7.1 speed install. I also froze hero v3.7.2, which answers the orchestrator's question with a yes: hold back two more images. Both went to [Small Talk — Orchestrator](#local_e4896004-68cd-4d55-9d37-ab925783b63b).

**The five checks:**
1. **Home-page sections and dashed lines:** these sections already clipped anything spilling past their edges, so skipping off-screen work cuts nothing new. The wavy section joins and the dashed line across them look intact.
2. **Hero start-up order:** the finger image and the first set's nails are preloaded and load first. The other six nail images start only after the finger arrives. The animation pauses when the menu opens and resumes when it closes. I couldn't watch the full start-up live because the browser pane was hidden, which stalls image decoding. The lab tests cover that part.
3. **Accessibility fix:** the finger wrapper is no longer hidden from screen readers, and the finger image is. The press-and-hold button can be reached by keyboard, and holding Space pauses the animation.
4. **Product-page illustration slides:** the wrist now ends at the slide's top-right corner on all seven sets.
5. **"Shop all nails" tile:** its nails fade in over 0.25 s, instantly for people who prefer reduced motion. The tile sits at the fold at 390, so there's no visible empty flash.

**Why v3.7.2:** the first set's character image (76 KB) and the preview hand (37 KB) still downloaded alongside the finger image on a slow connection. Holding them should make the finger appear about half a second sooner. The cost is that they fade in 0.25 s after the finger, which nobody will notice on a fast connection.
- **For st-foundation:** the template gives both images their address in a holding attribute instead of the normal one. The hero copies it over once the finger has loaded.
- **Our Vision tile:** the same idea applies there, so I suggested treating it like the "Shop all nails" tile. That tile isn't part of the hero, so it needs nothing from me.

In the lab, both images stay hidden until the finger loads. They always show the current set even if the set changes first, and they fade in as intended.

2. **Inner footer** (Journal, Our Story, Help, the talks): directly under the footer logo, lined up with its left edge. That space is empty today, so the footer doesn't grow. The icon is 20 px, close to the board's 18.
3. **Compact footer** (shop, product page, bag, Nail Guide): beside "Sign in" on the last row, 12 px to its right, with the pair kept centred. The icon is 20 px, and the footer doesn't grow.

On desktop each footer keeps the same relative placement.

### Assistant · 2026-10-10 14:28:08

The laptop and desktop spec for the home-page chapters is ready for st-foundation to build, about an hour after the ask. I sent it to [Small Talk — Orchestrator](#local_e4896004-68cd-4d55-9d37-ab925783b63b). The spec is [CHAPTERS-DESKTOP-SPEC.md](qa/desktop/CHAPTERS-DESKTOP-SPEC.md), and the prototype styles are in [st-landing-desktop-proto.css](qa/desktop/st-landing-desktop-proto.css). It applies from 1024 px wide; phones don't change.

**The layout matches the new desktop hero: art on the left, text on the right.**
- **One screen per chapter** under the header, capped at 900 px tall, so the name and pill can no longer fall below the fold.
- **The text block is the phone layout, moved and resized.** The handwritten lines, slogan, nails, highlighted name, pill and caption keep their phone arrangement. The block sits in the right half at about 1.2× phone size, down from 1.4×, which answers "huge headline". It's centred vertically in the screen.
- **The art fills the left half at up to 1.6× phone size,** answering "empty, sparse" and "small and cornered". Each piece stays pinned to the screen edge its cut edge belongs to, so no cut edge ever shows mid-screen.
  - **Diet Cherry and On Me:** the woman sits on the left, while the can or receipt hand stays on the right edge.
  - **Shaadi Shift and Pinky Promise:** their free side fades out softly.
  - **Green Flag:** on desktop it uses the hero's receiver-and-arm image, flipped as in the hero. The home-page woman and phone body are cut on opposite sides, so splitting them would break the phone cord.
- **The wavy joins between sections stay seamless.** The dashed decorative lines are hidden on desktop, because their paths are drawn for the phone width; desktop versions would be new art for later.

**Prototype test:** I tried the layout live on the Brainwave chapter at 1536×703 by injecting it into my own preview, then removed it. It fit one screen, with the pill ending at 628 of 703 px. The test also showed that a single centred art frame puts a cut edge mid-screen, which is why the spec pins each piece to its own edge.

st-foundation checks it at 1280×720, 1366×768, 1440×800 and 1536×703:
- each chapter fits one screen;
- no text over art;
- no visible cut edges;
- seamless joins;
- the highlighted name and the On Me and Pinky Promise rows unchanged.

I accept it after they install it. The cream sections and the rest of the store wait for the QA session's laptop audit.

I wrote the whole-store desktop spec as [qa/desktop/STORE-DESKTOP-SPEC.md](qa/desktop/STORE-DESKTOP-SPEC.md) and sent it to st-orchestrator for st-foundation to build after the chapters window. It's a spec only: nothing is built or checked on the preview yet, and I didn't write to the theme.

**What it covers.** Every section the laptop audit flagged, at 1024 px and wider. Phones are untouched, and widths from 990 to 1023 keep today's rules. It sits alongside hero v3.8 and the chapters spec.

**Shared rules**
- **Page frame:** content sits in a centred frame up to 1240 px wide with side margins, so no section shows a phone-width column with empty space beside it.
- **Two columns:** used wherever a section mixes two kinds of content (words and pictures, a list and a form, a list and a side panel).
- **Type:** headings 1.15× the phone size and a 60–72 character line length. The whole phone layout is never just scaled up, which is what caused the huge headline.
- **Landing cream sections:** built the same way as the chapters, with the shared `--kt` unit so the joins between sections stay seamless. The beelines are hidden on desktop, as in the chapters.

**Landing sections**
- **Tiles:** the two tiles side by side, 300–420 px wide each.
- **Talks teaser and Journal teaser:** heading on the left, the example talk or the two story cards on the right.
- **Nail Guide teaser:** the "Open the guide" button moves above the fold (it's below at 3 of the 4 audited sizes today).
- **FAQ:** heading and "Shop all sets" button on the left, the questions on the right.
- **Footer:** three columns (logo, tagline and Instagram | links | legal and ©), which fixes the logo stranded on the far left.

**Store pages**
- **Help, talks hub and thread:** main content on the left, with the contact form or the "Start a talk" panel staying in view on the right as you scroll. The thread is only 21–25% of the width today; it widens to fill the left column and the avatar goes to 96 px.
- **Journal:** the index becomes a card grid (two columns, three at 1360 px and up). Each story puts the hero art on the left, held in view, and the text on the right; today the art shows as a huge flat block above the text.
- **Our Story and Nail Guide:** words on one side, pictures on the other; the guide steps alternate sides.
- **Bag:** the "Need a hand?" and promo cards sit side by side under the items.
- **Search:** results use the shop's four-column grid.
- **404:** a two-column layout with a character image.
- **PDP and Shop:** the shop needs no change; the product page keeps its layout with a slightly larger gallery.

**How I'll accept it.** Once st-foundation has built it, I'll re-run the audit's checks at 1280×720, 1366×768, 1440×800 and 1536×703. The bar:
- no narrow centre columns;
- no landing headings or buttons below the fold;
- the first screen of each long page shows the heading and real content side by side;
- no sideways scroll;
- side panels never cover content;
- tap targets at least 44 px;
- the phone at 390×844 unchanged.

Next for me: accepting hero v3.8 and the chapters on the preview once they're installed.

### Assistant · 2026-10-10 15:06:04

The staged chapters build shouldn't be installed as it is: I wrote a v1.1 fix and told st-orchestrator to grant only once st-foundation has applied it and its own check passes. The fix is the new "v1.1" section at the top of [CHAPTERS-DESKTOP-SPEC.md](qa/desktop/CHAPTERS-DESKTOP-SPEC.md).

The orchestrator's read was right: on the owner's 1536×703 laptop, four of the seven women were small fragments in the bottom-left corner.

**Why it happened:** the build kept each piece at its phone position, at most about 1.5× bigger. Diet Cherry, Brainwave and On Me are half-face cut-outs by design, so at that size each filled only the bottom third of the left column. Only Green Flag, Wild Card and the Pinky scene have whole-figure versions, and those are already in use. So the fix is sizing, not swapping images.

**What v1.1 changes:**
- **Art sized to the screen:** each chapter's art is laid out as one group and scaled to the screen height. It only shrinks when the left column is narrow. The spec gives a per-piece table of sizes and positions (Green Flag, the Diet Cherry can and the On Me receipt are unchanged).
- **Copy moves left:** the text block shifts slightly left, closing the empty band in the middle.
- **Copy size cap 1.2 → 1.3:** next to the bigger art, 1.2 looked small. 1.3 balances without looking like the "huge headline" the owner complained about; that came from the old single centred column at 1.39 with nothing beside it.

**How I checked it:** I rendered st-foundation's lab page headless with my CSS injected, without changing their files. I checked 1536×703, 1280×720, 1366×768, 1440×800 and 1024×768:
- every woman now fills the left column at full height, and Brainwave and Wild Card read as composed scenes;
- the text keeps at least 39 px above and below it;
- the art stays at least 25 px clear of the text, and the can and receipt at least 16 px;
- no sideways scroll and no errors;
- phones and the 990–1023 band are untouched.

**One weak spot:** on the 4:3 screen at 1024×768, the narrow column holds Shaadi and Pinky to about 0.7 of full size, so they sit lower with plain colour above. I accepted that as the edge case; it's still bigger than the staged build.

**What st-foundation needs to do:** the prototype CSS targets pieces by position for testing, so they'll need to turn the per-piece table into real classes. They also need to re-measure the can and receipt clearance at the new 1.3 copy size; with the current figures the receipt is exactly at the 16 px minimum at 1280×720.

Sheets for each size are in `qa/desktop/v11/v11-sheet-<size>.png`, and the 1.2 vs 1.3 comparison is the `kc13-*` vs `v11-*` shots in `qa/desktop/v11/shots/`. I'll accept on the preview once it's installed.

# Desktop landing chapters (≥1024): existing approved art candidates

This is st-artwork's read-only inventory for st-fable's composition spec. No new art. Raw data is in `art-inventory.json` here, produced by `artwork/scripts/art_inventory.py`.

**How to read the columns:**
- **Edges:** which image borders carry an opaque *cut*. A cut must sit on a viewport or section edge (bleed), or be hidden behind something.
  - "free" = a full silhouette that can float anywhere.
  - "feathered" = the cut already fades out.
- **Max CSS width:** the largest width that stays sharp at 2× (px ÷ 2); never stretch beyond it. At ≥1024 the chapter is usually 2× DPR, but laptops at 1.25–1.5× get more headroom.
- **Landing:**
  - "chapter" = already used in that set's landing chapter.
  - "hero" = used only in the hero.
  - "—" = not on the landing.

### Assistant · 2026-10-10 17:36:48

The screenshots for the owner's new direction are ready in `qa/desktop/owner-v12/`, and I've told the orchestrator so it can pass them on. Nothing is installed: I injected the changes into the build preview in a headless browser, without writing to the theme. Each sheet shows the current landing on the left and the proposal on the right, as the full scroll and as one screen per chapter, at 390×844, 1536×703 and 1280×720. [README.md](qa/desktop/owner-v12/README.md) explains what to look at.

**Laptop chapters.** The art no longer always sits on the left; the seven chapters alternate:

| Chapter | Layout | Art |
|---|---|---|
| Diet Cherry | Text centred, art both sides | The woman on the left; the hand holding the Diet Coke can (borrowed from the hero) rising on the right |
| Brainwave | Text left, art right | The woman flipped to the right edge, with the sketchbook beside her |
| Green Flag | Art left | Unchanged |
| Shaadi Shift | Text left, art right | The dupatta flipped to the right edge |
| On Me | Text centred, art both sides | The receipt hand, much larger, on the right |
| Wild Card | Text left, art right | The woman flipped, with the cards beside her |
| Pinky Promise | Art left | Unchanged |

- Every piece is art the store already has; st-artwork listed the candidates in the same folder.
- The accepted rules still hold: one screen per chapter, no text over a face, the name and Shop button visible, and every image cut on a screen edge.
- Between 1024 and 1279 px wide there's no room for art on both sides, so Diet Cherry and On Me keep today's layout there. I haven't rendered that width range.

**Beeline.**
- **One line:** it's now a single dashed line down the whole landing page.
- **Through the slogans:** in each chapter it threads through the gap between the two slogan lines, behind the letters, so it reads as running through the campaign header.
- **Between the text blocks:** it then curves past the nails and around the name and Shop button, into the art and on to the next section.
- **Curves:** it no longer hugs the corners or runs in long straight lines.
- **Cream sections:** it runs under "the talks", between the two Journal lines and through "Find your fit.".
- **Layering:** it sits behind the art and text, so it never crosses a face or a button.
- **Laptop:** it has its own route, weaving between the art side and the text side and going around the handwritten notes.

**Trade-offs:**
- The new beeline is drawn by a script, so without JavaScript the page has no beeline at all, where today it falls back to a stretched copy.
- On laptops, moving the women and props to the right means flipping the artwork horizontally. Look closely at that when you review: a flipped face can read slightly differently.

Once the owner approves, st-foundation builds it from the README's implementation section, and I'll accept the result against these screenshots.

I've written the v12.1 spec from the owner's feedback and briefed st-foundation directly, copying st-orchestrator. st-artwork has the size and placement for the ace and king cards. Everything is lab renders on the build preview so far: nothing is installed, and I accept from after-shots once st-foundation builds it.

The spec is the new "v12.1" section at the top of [README.md](qa/desktop/owner-v12/README.md). The lab renders match what will be built, current on the left and proposed on the right: `OWNER121-scroll-*`, `OWNER121-chapters-*`, and `OWNER121-wildcard-cards-*` for the Wild Card close-ups.

/*
 * Small Talk hero motion controller.
 * Upgrades every [data-st-hero] root. Static Liquid first paint is never required to wait for this file.
 *
 * Principles
 * - Every flight is a Web Animations API animation on transform/opacity only (compositor), never per-frame JS.
 * - Flyers live inside the hero and are positioned in hero-local coordinates measured from the offset chain,
 *   so page scroll can never detach a nail. Ancestors of nail elements must not carry CSS transforms.
 * - Pausing (hold, user, hidden tab, offscreen, assets) pauses the running animations in place.
 * - Finite autoplay: at most MAX_SETS sets per pass, then settle. Manual navigation reaches all sets.
 * - Reduced motion: no flights, instant manual changes, autoplay never starts.
 */
(() => {
  'use strict';

  const ROOT = '[data-st-hero]';
